raw_response:
I am already old, so I do not want to gamble too much this year. My land is only 18 mu, and with some people working outside, the farm work still depends mainly on family timing. So I will keep the main land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steadiest way here. Wheat gives me a safe harvest, and maize follows right after, so even if one side is not very good, I still have another crop. Cotton and chili I will keep on smaller pieces. Cotton is slower but I know how to manage it, and chili can bring cash if the price is decent, but it needs more labor and more careful spraying, so I will not plant too much.

With my middle-school background, I do listen a bit to what the extension people say, but I still farm mostly from what I have seen on my own land and what nearby farmers do. Last year fertilizer helped, but water and fertilizer both cost money, so I will not push too hard. For wheat I will use a moderate base fertilizer and one topdress at jointing. For maize I will put most fertilizer near planting and add a little later if the stand looks strong. Cotton and chili need more watching for insects and disease, so I will budget some pesticide there. Since I have well irrigation, I can save the crop in a dry spell, but pumping costs money, so I will irrigate at key stages, not every time the soil looks a little dry.
